Project example 02 · Working together over decades

What applies today
must make sense tomorrow.

The Albrecht edition grows with every volume. People leave, procedures change and new findings emerge. Git preserves the history of files. But who explains which workflow is currently authoritative?

1Project2Perspective3Learning question4Your action

01

A project for generations

A consortium is editing Johann Friedrich Albrecht’s works, letters and papers. Volume teams have their own responsibilities, while registers, rules and outputs are connected. A publisher produces the books. The undertaking will outlast its current team.

02

A handbook belongs in the project from the start

Nora introduces a new colleague to the work. Samir sets up the approved working environment. The shared Git handbook explains tasks, checks, approval and where to get help. Its current version is maintained in the standards repository. Onboarding also includes practical Git training.

03

BUG-58 leads to handbook 1.1

After a faulty reimport, the team adds a check of characters and date-range markup immediately after the return transfer. Register annotations and dependent outputs are checked against the same version. The short-term rule goes straight into the handbook; a repair of the comment tool is commissioned at the same time. The two measures complement each other.

Before · 1.0

Check characters and date ranges before the handover.

Now · 1.1

Check characters and date-range markup after reimport; check dependent outputs against the same version.

Remember

A recorded history does not replace maintained working rules. The handbook and the people responsible for it belong in the Git strategy.

How we would proceed

  1. Bring current rules, examples and responsibilities together in one authoritative handbook.
  2. Review and approve workflow changes together with the handbook update.
  3. Ask a newcomer to follow the workflow from a fresh copy.

Done when: The newcomer can find and follow the current procedure and address a reasoned question to the responsible role.

A question for discussion

What would a new colleague understand tomorrow if all they received were the repository and our handbook?
